errors.english: refers to one or two words unread
errors.why: The Tibetan only opens the gloss on tshang, which continues on the next side ('...is an abode'); 'one or two words unread' is invented.

note: A generally faithful rendering of a word-by-word Vinaya commentary, with a misidentified object and an invented ending.

errors.english: because a perishing agent does not remain precisely because it remains as itself
errors.why: The point is that when the destroying factor is absent the thing remains of itself, so no separate cause of remaining is needed; the English is self-contradictory.

errors.english: If the support makes a state of perishing
errors.why: The support would cause the perishable thing to endure (gnas byed), not make 'a state of perishing'.
bskal/bskyal pa means the two faults were levelled against (imposed on) the opponent's position, not averted.

note: Follows the commentary closely in places but garbles the key argument about causes of endurance and inverts the faults imposed.

errors.english: (Upali) The Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of Vinaya or monastic discipline replied, "It should be given."
errors.why: Upāli is the one asking; the Buddha answers, addressing him: 'Upāli, it should be given.'

fix.find: (Upali) The Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of Vinaya or monastic discipline replied, "It should be given."
fix.replace: The Buddha replied, "Upāli, it should be given."

errors.english: such a son will not return to being the master of the father's house
errors.why: The son is not thereby excluded from ownership of the father's house, which is why one may accept from him; the English inverts it.

fix.find: such a son will not return to being the master of the father's house
fix.replace: such a son does not thereby cease to be an owner of the father's house

note: Readable Vinaya commentary, but the quoted Vinaya exchange is misassigned and the reasoning on the expelled son is inverted.

errors.english: the ascetic became convinced of his virtues and thought
errors.why: It is the king who becomes convinced that the ascetic has virtues and who then thinks and questions the Bodhisattva.

fix.find: the ascetic became convinced of his virtues and thought
fix.replace: the king became convinced of the ascetic's virtues and thought

note: Good verse rendering of the Kṣāntivādin episode, with the king's reaction misattributed to the ascetic.

errors.english: Except for the plants that do not grow, all others should be removed.
errors.why: Continuing the previous side, this concerns grass in which living creatures (srog chags) have not bred; it is not about plants that do not grow.

errors.english: The clay materials used for cleaning should be placed in earthenware shards.
errors.why: lci ba is cow-dung, kept as material for plastering/smearing, not clay for cleaning.
gnas 'char bcug means Udāyin had them take dependence (niśraya) on himself, i.e. made them his pupils.

note: Sound translation of the walkway rules and the opening of the eviction narrative, with a few misread practical and Vinaya terms.
A broadly faithful rendering of a difficult passage on toll evasion and boundaries; the remaining rough spots reflect an obscure Tibetan text.
A faithful, literal rendering of the Madhyamaka argument that the mind of the three times is not the object of self-grasping.

errors.english: The cause of realizing pervasion is the time of what has arisen and what will arise
errors.why: The sentence says that what is understood as pervading the times of both the arisen and the yet-to-arise is the cause; the English makes the time into the cause of realizing pervasion.

note: Good handling of the Pramāṇa dialectic on past and future causes, with one restructured sentence.

errors.english: Harmonious factors are not those of a similar class
errors.why: The gloss says the homogeneous factors ARE those of the same class, which is why they are the constituents.

fix.find: Harmonious factors are not those of a similar class
fix.replace: Harmonious factors are those of a similar class

errors.english: it would be because the sequential itself appears as the (actual thing)
errors.why: These are two separate word glosses ('if the other' = if the non-sequential appears; 'its own reality appears' = by the sequence itself appearing), not one causal statement.

errors.english: means it does not abide in the cognition of the object of appraisal
errors.why: The gloss says it refers to what abides in the cognition of the object; the negation is added.

note: A word-gloss commentary handled patiently but with an inverted opening definition and some misjoined glosses.

errors.english: Others, not understanding this intention, have spoken about "externalists" [note: original: "phyi rol pa rnams", likely referring to those who posit real universals outside the mind]
errors.why: Lest others miss the intention, the author says 'those that are external', which the next sentence glosses as the particulars (external to the universal); it is neither a statement by others nor a reference to realist opponents.

note: Accurate on the apoha-related argument about conceptual cognition, with one misread root-text lemma and a misleading note.
